ctx.x: Did he sound anything like Buck?
Well, something like Buck. Buck Johnson. Yeah, some, some phrases. Yeah. Yeah, some like Lewis Armstrong. Yeah. And then he had a good many ideas of his own. Yes. Frazes.

There was some, you know, there's some story I read in some book somewhere that there's a chance that he may have made some home accordings in Thibodeau. Did you ever hear anything about that? No, I didn't. I haven't heard anything about any of his recordings. I mean, nobody's ever found them, you know? No, well, I, I, I don't know. It's just a rumor that they may exist. I was just wondering if you may have heard something about that. Did he ever play out there? Thibodeau? Yeah.

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: Now he, he and Louis Armstrong come up together back there in the Joneses home.

ctx.x: George Washington. One of these times. Now he, he and Louis Armstrong come up together back there in the Joneses home. He could play a baritone, bass on, and trombone. Mm-hmm. And he was good. See, I don't see nothing in that book. You know, I'll show you that book I have. No. I got a book of, you know, old musicians.
Which book is it? What color is it?
